raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3's sparse-attention Triton kernels re-run their autotune sweeps on every server start, even with a warm `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, because none of the 9 `@triton.autotune` decorators under `minimax_sparse/` set `cache_results`; this sets it, so a restart loads the saved winners instead of re-sweeping during CUDA-graph capture.

## Modifications

- Add `**autotune_cache_kwargs` to all 9 autotune decorators in `minimax_sparse/{decode,prefill}/`, reusing the helper the FLA and Mamba SSD kernels already use. Configs and keys are unchanged. `FLA_CACHE_RESULTS=0` turns it off, and it is a no-op on a Triton without `cache_results`.
- Add `test_sparse_autotuners_cache_results` to `test_minimax_sparse_gqa.py`. Run out of tree on CPU, it fails on main (9/9 uncached) and on two partial variants: one that misses the functional-style `_gqa_share_sparse_decode_kernel`, and one that leaves the prefill decorators uncached. It passes with this PR.

Trade-off: the cache freezes the first sweep's pick for each key. At TP8, one cold sweep picked `num_warps=8, num_stages=3` for batch bucket 64, while main picked `num_stages=2` in 4 of 4 sweeps. Every later restart then ran gqa decode 6.8 % / 7.6 % slower at bs 37 / 61, until the cache was cleared or `FLA_CACHE_RESULTS=0` was set. This is the same exposure the FLA and Mamba kernels already have.

## Accuracy Tests

TBD: GSM8K A/B pending.

Autotune only selects `num_warps`/`num_stages`. In the op-level run below, `topk_idx` and the decode output at bs 1/3/37 were bit-identical to main at TP1 and TP8.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Op-level startup walk: 1 prefill, then the 52 CUDA-graph capture sizes from 512 down to 1, with MiniMax-M3 head layouts. Setup:

- MI355X (gfx950), main@d9521615b7 (these files are unchanged up to b45a36531c), Triton 3.8.0.
- Each arm ran as 4 fresh processes with a per-arm `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, wiped before run 1.
- Figures are the median of runs 2–4, with [min–max].

| Walk time (s) | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP1 (64q/4kv), warm restart | 9.19 [9.14–9.39] | 0.89 [0.88–0.99] | −90.3 % |
| TP8 (8q/1kv), warm restart | 8.03 [8.01–8.18] | 0.89 [0.88–1.01] | −88.9 % |
| TP1, first cold start | 89.4 | 93.0 | — |
| TP8, first cold start | 83.1 | 82.9 | — |

There is no gain on the first cold start. Steady-state gqa decode under HIP graph stayed within main's own run-to-run config-selection noise, except for the TP8 bs 37–61 case above. Only MiniMax-M3 / M3.1 (`MiniMaxM3Sparse*`) reach these kernels. On MI355X (TP8, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`) the sweeps that run by default are the gqa decode kernel and the two prefill indexer kernels; on NVIDIA, Blackwell uses MSA and Hopper paged decode is pinned, so little of this is reached there.

e2e: TBD.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -9,10 +9,24 @@
 
 import pytest
 import torch
+from triton.runtime.autotuner import Autotuner, Heuristics
 
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.utils import SUPPORTS_AUTOTUNE_CACHE
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.minimax_sparse.decode import (
+    flash_with_topk_idx as decode_flash_with_topk_idx,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.minimax_sparse.decode import (
+    topk_sparse as decode_topk_sparse,
+)
 from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.minimax_sparse.decode.topk_sparse import (
     flash_decode_with_gqa_share_sparse,
 )
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.minimax_sparse.prefill import (
+    flash_with_topk_idx as prefill_flash_with_topk_idx,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.minimax_sparse.prefill import (
+    topk_sparse as prefill_topk_sparse,
+)
 from sglang.srt.utils import get_device
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
 
@@ -363,5 +377,28 @@ def test_sparse_gqa_deterministic(bs, nqh, nkh, hd, blk, tk, with_sink, seq_pat,
     )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not SUPPORTS_AUTOTUNE_CACHE, reason="triton.autotune has no cache_results"
+)
+def test_sparse_autotuners_cache_results():
+    """Every sparse-attention autotuner must persist its winner across restarts."""
+    autotuners = {}
+    for module in (
+        decode_flash_with_topk_idx,
+        decode_topk_sparse,
+        prefill_flash_with_topk_idx,
+        prefill_topk_sparse,
+    ):
+        for name, kernel in vars(module).items():
+            while isinstance(kernel, Heuristics):
+                kernel = kernel.fn
+            if isinstance(kernel, Autotuner):
+                autotuners[f"{module.__name__}.{name}"] = kernel
+
+    assert autotuners
+    uncached = [name for name, kernel in autotuners.items() if not kernel.cache_results]
+    assert not uncached, uncached
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "-s"]))
